question: A portable CMS designer proposes 'DLY' to mean DELAY. Using Section 1D.08 and Table 1D-3, is this acceptable and why?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No, "DLY" is not acceptable. Table 1D-3 lists DLY as an unacceptable abbreviation for "Delay" because road users commonly misinterpret it as "Daily," and Section 1D.08 makes clear that abbreviations in Table 1D-3 shall not be used on any traffic control device, including portable CMS. Standards (mandatory): - "The abbreviations shown in Table 1D-3 shall not be used in connection with traffic control devices because of their potential to be misinterpreted by road users." - "When the word messages shown in Table 1D-2 need to be abbreviated on a portable changeable message sign, the abbreviations shown in Table 1D-2 shall be used. Unless indicated by an asterisk, these abbreviations shall only be used on portable changeable message signs." - "Abbreviations displayed on CMS shall comply with the provisions of Section 1D.08." Guidance (recommended): - The abbreviations for words listed in Table 1D-2 that show a prompt word should not be used on a portable changeable message sign unless the prompt word shown in Table 1D-2 either precedes or follows the abbreviation, as applicable — reinforcing that only sanctioned abbreviations with proper context should appear on a CMS. - If Table 1D-1 or 1D-2 allows more than one abbreviation for a word or phrase, the same abbreviation should be used throughout a single jurisdiction. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Table 1D-3 explicitly lists "DLY" with intended word "Delay" and common misinterpretation "Daily," confirming it is an unacceptable abbreviation. [Image 2] Table 1D-2 (Sheet 1 of 2) lists the abbreviations that shall be used on portable CMS, and "DLY"/"Delay" does not appear as an approved entry. [Image 3] Page 37 shows Table 1D-3 in full context, with DLY → Delay/Daily among the prohibited abbreviations. [Image 5] Page 34 shows Section 1D.08, including the Standard that Table 1D-3 abbreviations shall not be used because of their potential misinterpretation. [Image 6] Page 516 shows Section 2L.05's Standard that abbreviations displayed on CMS shall comply with Section 1D.08. Citations: - Section 1D.08 Standard §4 (p.34) - Section 1D.08 Standard §2 (p.34) - Section 2L.05 Standard §6 (p.516) - Section 1D.08 Guidance §3 (p.34) - Section 1D.08 Guidance §5 (p.34) - Table 1D-3 (p.37) - Table 1D-2 (p.36)
gold_answer: No. DLY is explicitly prohibited because it can be misinterpreted as DAILY.
